articles.headline: Guard Sam Cosmi, safety Nick Cross out for London game vs. Colts
articles.description: Commanders guard Sam Cosmi and safety Nick Cross did not travel with the team to London on Tuesday night for their Week 4 game against the Colts.
articles.headlineJa: ガードのサム・コスミとセーフティのニック・クロス、コルツとのロンドン戦を欠場
articles.descriptionJa: コマンダースのガード、サム・コスミとセーフティのニック・クロスは、第4週のコルツ戦に向けて火曜夜に行われたチームのロンドン遠征に同行しませんでした。
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders ruled out two starters for Sunday's game in London, though three others remain a possibility to return. Guard Sam Cosmi and safety Nick Cross did not travel with the team to London on Tuesday night for their Week 4 game against the Colts.

Both were considered long shots to make the trip; each was hurt in Week 2 at Dallas. Cosmi suffered a concussion late in the 37-20 loss while Cross played despite an injury the team has described as "internal" but needed to have surgery after the game and stayed overnight at a hospital in Dallas.

Three other injured starters did accompany Washington (1-2) to London, as coach Dan Quinn said they would on Monday: quarterback Jayden Daniels (elbow), tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) and linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin). Quinn said all three would participate in at least some portion of practice this week. Washington will have a light workout Wednesday after arriving earlier that morning.

Daniels sustained his injury in Week 2 but is considered week-to-week. Because it's to his left and non-throwing elbow, he has already resumed some throwing. Marcus Mariota would start against the Colts if Daniels can't play.

If Luvu can't play, then Kain Medrano would start alongside rookie Sonny Styles. Both players intercepted a pass in Sunday's 33-31 win over Seattle. Medrano, a 2025 fifth-round pick, returned his 50 yards for a touchdown. He opened the season as the Commanders' fifth inside linebacker and a special teams performer, but injuries forced him into his first snaps from scrimmage in the NFL. Leo Chenal fractured his neck in that win and Jordan Magee injured his hamstring in Week 1 and is on injured reserve.

Okonkwo, like Luvu, has missed the last two weeks.

With Cosmi once again sidelined, Nick Allegretti is expected to start at right guard with veteran Lucas Patrick at center. Patrick, signed after Week 1, left Sunday's win with a boot on his left foot. He missed four snaps during the game because of an ankle injury.

articles.headline: Man City's Elliot Anderson no handball call was correct - PL panel
articles.description: The referee and VAR were correct to rule that Manchester City's Elliot Anderson did not handle the ball against Sunderland, a Premier League panel ruled.
articles.headlineJa: マン・シティのエリオット・アンダーソンにハンドを取らなかった判定は正当、PLパネルが結論
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグのパネルは、サンダーランド戦でマンチェスター・シティのエリオット・アンダーソンがハンドを犯さなかったとした主審とVARの判定は正しかったと判定した。
articles.body:
Referee Rob Jones and VAR Michael Salisbury were correct to rule that Manchester City midfielder Elliot Anderson did not handle the ball in his side's thrilling 5-3 win over Sunderland, according to a Premier League panel.

The Black Cats were furious after the ball hit Anderson's hand as he challenged Enzo Le Fée in the City penalty area during a breathless second half.

Jones waved away protests and Salisbury did not overrule him from Stockley Park, which angered Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris.

However, Premier League's Key Match Incidents five-person panel agreed with the on-field decision by a majority of three to two.

Two people on the panel made up of three former players and coaches, a Premier League representative and one from Pro Ref felt that Anderson deliberately moved his arm towards the ball.

The panel's findings read: "The referee's call of no penalty for a potential handball offence against Anderson was supported, 3:2.

"Both players were engaged and the ball was bouncing at close proximity after deflecting off Le Fee.

"Two panellists felt that there was a deliberate secondary movement of the arm from Anderson that was a handball offence."

The panel also voted four to one in ruling VAR's decision not to intervene as correct.

There was also a split decision over Everton's disallowed goal in their 1-0 win over Ipswich at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

- Man City to appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case

- Thomas Tuchel 'did not talk' to England's Man City players about guilty verdict

- Roy Keane: I'd put Man City medals 'in the bin' after 'cheating'

The Toffees thought they had doubled their lead when Thierno Barry headed home, but referee Stuart Attwell was advised Brennan Johnson was offside in front of goalkeeper Christian Walton.

The ruling read: "The VAR intervention to disallow the goal for interfering with an opponent by Johnson was supported, 3:2.

"Johnson was clearly in an offside position, in very close proximity to the goalkeeper and makes a movement, impacting the goalkeeper's ability to set and move to the ball. Two panellists felt that Johnson's position and actions did not impact goalkeeper Walton."

articles.headline: Barcelona chief explains how Lautaro Martínez pursuit ended over a phone call
articles.description: Joan Laporta has confirmed Barcelona tried to sign Lautaro Martínez this summer but quickly gave up once it became apparent Inter Milan would not allow the striker to leave.
articles.headlineJa: バルサ会長、ラウタロ・マルティネス獲得の試みが1本の電話で終了した経緯を明かす
articles.descriptionJa: ジョアン・ラポルタ会長は、バルセロナが今夏ラウタロ・マルティネスの獲得を試みたものの、インテル・ミラノが同ストライカーの放出を認めないことが明確になり、即座に断念したことを認めた。
articles.body:
Joan Laporta has confirmed Barcelona tried to sign Lautaro Martínez this summer but quickly gave up once it became apparent Inter Milan would not allow the striker to leave.

The Spanish champions spent the transfer window trying to sign a No.9, turning their attention to Martínez after failing to land Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez.

However, after reaching out to Inter CEO Giuseppe Marotta, Laporta realised a deal for the Argentina international would not be possible either, with Barça eventually signing Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal.

"One day I called Marotta," the Barça chief told Corriere della Sera. "It was he and I on the call -- no intermediaries -- and I told him I would have loved to have Lautaro on my team because I admire the guy so much.

"But Marotta didn't even let me finish speaking. He made it clear Lautaro wasn't for sale and that it wouldn't be up to the player to decide whether or not to move. So I stopped the whole line of thought. There was no way to take it any further."

Following the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres in the post-season, Barça were keen to bolster their attack with a new striker.

But despite signing Jesus on the final day of the transfer window, the solution has come in-house, with Raphinha being converted into a No.9 at the start of the new campaign.

The Brazil forward has quickly adapted to his new position, scoring 14 goals in eight appearances, including back-to-back LaLiga hat tricks before the international break.

It is not the first time Barça have tried to sign Martínez, who was also a target in 2020 when they were looking to replace Luis Suárez.

- Barcelona await updates after Brazil's Raphinha substituted due to thigh discomfort

- Kylian Mbappé, Ibrahima Konaté, Fede Valverde expected to be available for El Clásico - source

- Espanyol sporting director apologises for backing Lamine Yamal to win Ballon d'Or

Speaking earlier in September, Martínez said it was an "honour and a source of immense satisfaction" to be linked to clubs like Barça, but pledged his future to Inter. 

Martínez, who has four goals in four Serie A games this season, has a contract with the club until 2029.

Since signing for the Italian giants from Racing Club in 2018, he has netted 179 goals in 381 appearances, winning three Scudettos, three Coppas Italia and reaching two Champions League finals.

articles.headline: Can the 0-3 Texans defy history again to make playoffs?
articles.description: Houston became the first team in the common playoff format to make the postseason after starting 0-3 in 2025.
articles.headlineJa: 0勝3敗のテキサンズは再び歴史を覆してプレーオフに進出できるか？
articles.descriptionJa: ヒューストンは2025年、0勝3敗のスタートから現行のプレーオフ形式でポストシーズン進出を果たした初のチームとなった。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- Is it déjà vu for the Houston Texans?

The preseason Super Bowl contenders find themselves at 0-3 for the second straight year -- and the losses have come in similar fashion.

Last year, the Texans' first three games were lost on the last drive, and this season, the same happened in two of the three weeks.

Quarterback C.J. Stroud was sacked and fumbled inside the red zone on Houston's last drive against the Buffalo Bills in Week 1, and in Week 3, the Texans' defense allowed a game-winning field goal against the Indianapolis Colts with 16 seconds remaining.  

But Houston remains confident despite the frustration.

"We've been here before," Stroud said after the latest loss. "We can get these fixed, and we will." 

Like last season, Houston's offense hasn't been great. The unit is averaging 18 points (tied for 23rd) and 326 yards (14th in total offense). Stroud also has been sacked 10 times, tied for second most in the NFL.

They might have been able to circumvent history last year, but even that was a tall task. Entering this season, 25 teams had started 0-3 under the current playoff format (since 2020), and last year's Texans are the only one to reach the postseason, according to ESPN Research. Houston also became the seventh team in the Super Bowl era (1966) to reach the playoffs after 0-3, and the last team to do it before that was ... the 2018 Texans.

"In this league, no one cares about what happened," Stroud said. "They just want to see if you won or lost. So at the end of the day, we know who we are in our locker room. We know we will hear noise all week.

"But at the end of the day, it's us in the locker room."

The Texans started 3-5 last season before winning their final nine games, but slow starts have become a trend for Houston under coach DeMeco Ryans. In Ryans and Stroud's debut season in 2023, the Texans started 0-2. The only anomaly under Ryans is 2024, when they started 2-0. 

Still, the Texans have found a way to climb out of those holes -- reaching the divisional round of the playoffs during the past three years. But Ryans won't lean on past experiences because he believes each year is different.

"For me, if we're 0-3, obviously I haven't coached good enough," Ryans said. "So, haven't coached good enough. I've got to coach better. If I coach better, we'll find ourselves on the winning side."

The offense has sorely missed Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins, who had seven catches for 75 yards and a TD in the opener. After compiling 381 yards in the opener, Houston has averaged 298.5 yards (23rd) and scored 11.5 points (tied for 30th) without Collins (hamstring). 

Last year through three weeks, Houston's offense averaged 12.7 points (last), but its defense allowed 17 points (tied for fifth best). articles.headline: Can the Broncos keep pulling off unlikely comeback victories?
articles.description: Somehow, the Broncos keep finding ways to overcome their slow first-half starts, pulling off frenetic second-half comeback wins -- including in Week 3 against the Rams.
articles.headlineJa: ブロンコスは奇跡的な逆転勝利を収め続けることができるか？
articles.descriptionJa: ブロンコスは、第3週のラムズ戦を含め、前半のスロースタートを克服する方法をどうにか見つけ出し、後半の猛烈な逆転勝利を重ね続けている。
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- The Denver Broncos have found the most improbable comfort zone. This past Sunday night's 30-26 victory over the Los Angeles Rams was the fourth time in Sean Payton's three-plus-season tenure as head coach the Broncos have won a game in which they were behind 14 or more points in the second half.

"This team rises," safety Talanoa Hufanga said.

Quarterback Bo Nix added that team's high-wire dance "feels like our DNA."

Hufanga and Nix's comments form a pushback against proven concepts like regression to the mean or the thought that past results don't guarantee future performance. And yet another comeback win might be rejecting the common-sense belief that the Broncos can't keep winning in this fashion.

But this past Sunday was the 10th time since Nix was drafted in 2024 that the Broncos have produced a fourth-quarter comeback victory. And it marked the first time in franchise history the Broncos have had consecutive comeback wins in which they trailed by double-digits in the second half (Denver overcame a 10-point, third-quarter deficit to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 2).

The Broncos (2-1) have developed a reputation for being second-half escape artists. But as they get set to face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers (3-0) on the road Sunday (4:25 p.m. ET, Levi's Stadium, CBS), how do they really feel about their current trend of overcoming lackluster first halves to win in late, dramatic fashion?

Payton tried to add some perspective moments after the Rams win, saying that a start like the Broncos had against Los Angeles -- in which they were outgained 273-67 in the first half while falling behind 16-0 -- would be "something we're frustrated about later if we don't get it cleaned up." And "later" could mean as soon as Sunday, given 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy leads the NFL in QBR (93.8) and touchdown passes (nine) while throwing only one interception.

The 49ers lead the league in offensive efficiency by a margin of more than 14 points over the second-place Buffalo Bills, who are closer to seventh place than they are to San Francisco. The Niners also lead the NFL in offensive expected points added (EPA) by a little more than 15 points, with the No. 2 team (Buffalo) being closer to No. 8 than it is to the 49ers. So, the Broncos, who have scored only 10 first-half points this season, would rather not be forced rely on a third straight escape act.

"We'll look at the tape [of Sunday's win] and I'm sure and pull our hair out with some stuff," Payton said. "And be excited about some things, too"

While it's not ideal, the Broncos can be excited about their ability to recover and thrive in seemingly hopeless situations. And the win over the Rams was among their most improbable.

"I wouldn't say it's good to be familiar in those situations, but once you are in those situations, you're familiar and you have been in that environment before and you understand what it takes to overcome the situations," Broncos wide receiver

articles.headline: Why Geno Smith's hot start has been a bright spot for the Jets
articles.description: Despite being 1-2, the 35-year-old QB is completing over 75% of his passes.
articles.headlineJa: ジーノ・スミスの好スタートがジェッツにとっての明るい話題である理由
articles.descriptionJa: チームは1勝2敗にとどまっているものの、35歳のQBはパス成功率75%以上を記録している。
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- When the New York Jets traded for Geno Smith in March, bringing him back to where he started his career in 2013, it prompted a loud groan from their quarterback-scarred fanbase.

Smith 1.0 doesn't evoke fond memories for Jets fans, and his performance last season for the Las Vegas Raiders was so uneven that the franchise was willing to eat $16 million of his 2026 salary to have him play elsewhere.

Desperate for a bridge starter, the Jets took on the reclamation project, hoping he could recapture his Seattle Seahawks form -- circa 2022 when he led passers with over 100 attempts in completion percentage (69.8) -- and provide stability at their most unstable position.

Through three games, Smith, 35, has exceeded expectations in New York, giving off early comeback-season vibes.

"He's a warrior, man," tight end Jeremy Ruckert said. "He's a field general. We have the utmost confidence in him."

Smith's completion rating (75.5%) ranks second in the NFL, and he's giving credence to the slogan, "What happens in Vegas, stays in Vegas" -- which is to say, he's not throwing interceptions like he did as a member of the Raiders.

After a league-high 17 interceptions last season, Smith has yet to throw one in 102 pass attempts. The last time he went three straight games without a pick was the final three games of the 2023 season, his second year as the Seahawks' starter.

There's a lot of season left, but it's worth noting that Smith is putting up numbers that would rank among the best passing seasons in franchise history.

Disclaimer: It's not a glittering history. Beyond franchise icon Joe Namath, there's only a sprinkling of above-average to excellent seasons over the last half-century.

Only two players passed for 3,000 yards, 20 touchdowns and a 65% completion rate in the same season -- Chad Pennington (2002) and Brett Favre (2008). Mind you, these aren't extraordinary benchmarks. In today's NFL, they represent a solid season. In Favre's case, he had as many touchdown passes (22) as interceptions, which blemishes his season.

With 783 yards and four touchdowns, Smith is on pace to blow away those marks. Of course, perspective is important.

Smith has battled inconsistency at times in his career, and his current supporting cast is banged up. The status of running back Breece Hall (quad), wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) and tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) are uncertain as they prepare to face the Chicago Bears on Sunday at Soldier Field. Chances are, he won't have Hall, a blow to an already sputtering rushing attack.

That said, Smith has emerged as one of the early bright spots in the Jets' 1-2 start. On Sunday, he passed for 321 yards and three touchdowns in the 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions, the first Jets' quarterback since Mike White in 2022 to have 300 yards and three touchdowns in a game.

articles.headline: Man City should be stripped of titles - Jamie Carragher
articles.description: Manchester City should be stripped of the titles won during the period where they have been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules, Jamie Carragher said
articles.headlineJa: ジェイミー・キャラガー氏「マンチェスター・シティはタイトルを剥奪されるべき」
articles.descriptionJa: ジェイミー・キャラガー氏は、マンチェスター・シティがプレミアリーグの財務規則に違反したと認められた期間に獲得したタイトルについて、剥奪されるべきだと述べました。
articles.body:
Manchester City should be stripped of the titles won during the period where they have been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules, Jamie Carragher said

City were found to have engaged in an almost £1 billion scheme to either inflate revenues or reduce costs through a series of "sham" arrangements in order to avoid breaching league and UEFA financial regulations.

The eight-time Premier League champions face severe sanctions, although City remain defiant and immediately declared their intention to appeal.

"I feel for the players... they'll almost feel like a lot of their career is going to have an asterisk, or a lot of people will be calling it a sham," Carragher said on Sky Sports News.

"The players were told everything was fine, they would never get done for anything. What the hierarchy are coming out with now, they're just gaslighting.

"I think the titles should be taken off their [City's] list. Whether other clubs get them is probably slightly different. City have not just hurt their own players.

"I don't look at it [a medal] years later, but my mind goes back to moments and feelings in my stomach. Those players will never get that feeling and it was robbed by Man City. No-one remembers the medal. Giving trophies or medals back, it doesn't mean anything. It's not about medals, it's about feelings."

City's next match comes in the Premier League on Oct. 11 against Liverpool, the club that have been their biggest rival across the last decade.

"Liverpool are probably the biggest losers in all this," Carragher added. "The atmosphere will be electric. In the last five years, Liverpool vs. Manchester City has been 'the' game of the Premier League."

Ex-City defender Micah Richards said on The Rest Is Football podcast: "The reports were troubling. I saw the words which were used by the Premier League in sham contracts and I felt absolutely devastated.

"I've been at that club since I was 14 years old, I would die for that club. I achieved my dream at Manchester City, but then to hear these reports, and not only me as an ex-player, but the fans, what they have to go through, absolutely devastating."

Richards described speaking to the fan he used to live with as a young player at the club, adding: "My digs man, he rang me and he was literally in tears and asking me about information, which I don't know, I haven't got the answers to tell him.

"And that's someone who's supported the club for 60-odd years, and the uncertainty around it is just heartbreaking.

articles.headline: Christian Izien stars in strong defensive week for NFL stars with Africa ties
articles.description: Detroit Lions safety Christian Izien - who is from Far Rockaway, Queens, but has always proudly represented Nigeria too - was a standout among many NFL stars with ties to Africa who shone in Week 3.
articles.headlineJa: アフリカにルーツを持つNFLスターが守備で躍動した週、クリスチャン・イジエンが大活躍
articles.descriptionJa: クイーンズのファー・ロッカウェイ出身ながら誇りを持ってナイジェリアも代表するデトロイト・ライオンズのセーフティ、クリスチャン・イジエンは、第3週に輝きを放ったアフリカにゆかりのある多くのNFLスターの中でも特に目立つ活躍を見せました。
articles.body:
Detroit Lions safety Christian Izien - who is from Far Rockaway, Queens, but has always proudly represented Nigeria too - was a standout among many NFL stars with ties to Africa who shone in Week 3.

There were some highlights on offense too - notably from Jaxon Smith-Njigba and John Metchie III - but generally, this was a week where defense shone brightest for the continent's stars.

Africa Player of the Week: Christian Izien (Detroit Lions)

Izien was immensely influential for the Detroit Lions in their 31-24 win over the New York Jets, making a total of 11 tackles - nine of which were solo tackles - and defending one pass.

Izien - who has family ties to Nigeria - made three tackles for loss in addition to a vital intervention to prevent a touchdown right on the stroke of half-time. Geno Smith went for a Hail Mary with the Jets 10-7 down, but amid a sea of bodies from both teams, it was Izien who got to the ball first to tip it away.

His performance played a key role in the game ending in favour of the Lions - who are 2-1 for the season, with the Jets 1-2.

Africa Moment of the Week: Thomas Incoom and Maema Njongmeta (Carolina Panthers)

There were plenty of big hits to choose from among Africa's NFL stars. However, Incoom (born in Ghana) and Njongmeta (born in Cameroon) get the nod for collaborating in a moment which demonstrated what Africa has to offer the NFL.

As their Carolina Panthers faced the Cleveland Browns, Njongmeta forced a fumble with a huge hit on Malachi Corley and then Incoom - who had earlier set the tone with a massive hit himself - was on hand for the fumble recovery.

Although the Browns ultimately emerged victorious 21-18, it was not for any want of trying from the West African duo.

Honorable mentions

Jaxon Smith-Njigba - who proudly represents Sierra Leone, with which he has ties through his grandparents - scored two touchdowns among a total of 10 receptions for 128 yards. His Seattle Seahawks lost 33-31 to the Washington Commanders despite his contribution on offense and Uchenna Nwosu (ties to Nigeria) defending a pass.

John Metchie III - who is of Nigerian and Taiwanese descent and lived in Ghana as a young child - scored a touchdown for the Panthers in their defeat to the Browns. Nigerian-American outside linebacker Princely Umanmielen also made a notable contribution even in defeat for the Panthers, picking up a sack.

Adetomiwa Adebawore deserves special mention for his 1.5 sacks for the Indianapolis Colts in their 19-17 win over the Houston Texans.

Ruke Orhorhoro (Jacksonville Jaguars), Ogbo Okoronkwo (San Francisco 49ers), Eyioma Uwazurike (Denver Broncos), and Dayo Odeyingbo (Chicago Bears) - all of Nigerian descent - all picked up sacks in Week 3 wins.

Osa Odighizuwa, who contributed to the Niners' 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals with a pass defended, also has ties to Nigeria.

So, too, do players who had impressive moments on both sides of the Buffalo Bills' 24-16 win over the LA Chargers - Davison

articles.headline: Man City to appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case
articles.description: Manchester City have until Friday to lodge an appeal against the guilty verdict handed down in their case with the Premier League and have stated publicly they intend to do so.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティ、プレミアリーグ違反問題での有罪判決に対し控訴へ
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティは、プレミアリーグの規約違反問題で下された有罪判決に対して金曜日までに控訴する必要があり、控訴する意向を公に表明しています。
articles.body:
Manchester City have until Friday to lodge an appeal against the guilty verdict handed down in their case with the Premier League and have stated publicly they intend to do so.

City's guilt in relation to "all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules" between 2009 and 2018 was detailed in a bombshell statement from the Premier League on Tuesday along with an accompanying written judgement from the independent commission which heard the case.

The Premier League said the "issue of sanction will be addressed separately in a further hearing with the independent commission."

In a statement issued on Tuesday, City said they will appeal the verdict.

It read: "Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

In a video message sent out to club employees after the publication of the verdict, CEO Ferran Soriano reiterated City's intention to fight on.

"The whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation," said Soriano.

"That the owner's personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true.

"Our lawyers will now file an appeal that sets out that the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact and is unsafe."

City have the right to appeal under Premier League rules, although the competition's statement on Tuesday made clear that they want a quick resolution after initially announcing charges against City in February 2023.

"The club has the right to appeal the independent Commission's findings and has until Friday, October 2 to exercise that right," the Premier League said in their lengthy statement on Tuesday. "The Premier League Board's intention is that the full process (including any appeals and publication of relevant decisions) is concluded as soon as possible."

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid eye Van Dijk on free transfer at end of season
articles.description: Real Madrid are hoping they can sign Virgil van Dijk when his Liverpool contract expires at the end of the season. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・最新情報：レアル・マドリードが今季終了時にフリーでファン・ダイク獲得を狙う
articles.descriptionJa: レアル・マドリードは、今シーズン終了時にリヴァプールとの契約が満了するフィルジル・ファン・ダイクの獲得を望んでいる。「Transfer Talk」が最新情報をお届け。
articles.body:
Real Madrid are hoping they can sign Virgil van Dijk when his Liverpool contract expires at the end of the season. Plus, Gilberto Mora is subject to interest from Liverpool.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool skipper Virgil van Dijk could join Real Madrid on a free transfer when his contract expires at the end of the 2026-27 season, according to Mundo Deportivo. The 35-year-old central defender has not received an offer of a renewal from Liverpool officials, suggesting that his time at the club could be coming to a natural conclusion. Madrid boss Jose Mourinho, who already has Van Dijk's former teammates Trent Alexander-Arnold and Ibrahima Konaté in his defensive ranks, both also signed at the end of their Liverpool contracts, is interested in adding another center back. However, Madrid are not the only club monitoring the situation, with AC Milan, Galatasaray and Inter Miami also mentioned as potential destinations. Van Dijk joined Liverpool in 2018 and helped transform the club's fortunes, playing his part in the club winning every domestic trophy as well as the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA World Club Cup.

- Liverpool are interested in Club Tijuana and Mexico international midfielder Gilberto Mora, according to Football Insider. The Reds are said to be admirers of the 17-year-old, but there is significant competition emerging in the race for his signature, with Real Madrid, Barcelona, and Paris Saint-Germain also keen. The Liga MX side are expected to part ways with him at the end of the season when they believe his value will be at its highest. Mora impressed at the World Cup in the summer and has made an impressive start to the new campaign with five goals in seven matches.

- Real Madrid are monitoring the situation of Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, TEAMtalk reports. Madrid are assessing the transfer market for a long-term option between the posts, and they see the 27-year-old as a strong candidate to succeed Thibaut Courtois due to his experience in the Champions League. Whether City part ways with Donnarumma could hinge on their punishment after they were found guilty on Tuesday of almost all 115 financial charges brought against them by the Premier League. City have until Friday to appeal.

- Barcelona defender Jules Koundé has been placed on the shortlist of Bayern Munich, Diario Sport reports. The Bundesliga club have kept close tabs on the 27-year-old for some time, and they are lining up an approach for him as a potential future successor to defender Kim Min-jae. Kounde signed a new five-year contract back in August 2025, but having failed to establish himself as a starter in La Liga this season, a switch to the Allianz Arena could become a possibility in the January transfer window.

- Manchester United are weighing up a move for Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta
